1. Local comparison changes the physical reference operation

The available metered-exchange construction uses six short opposing-shoe pods. Its actual optical range Jacobian differs from its support Jacobian. The calculated target deformations of 16.47,14.20,4.72,4.78,10.03,6.50um cannot be removed by calling raw range accuracy an installed rigid-pose accuracy. The return's .9554/.9878mm catch figures require an unproved corrected20um observation. Including raw error and target deformation gives .9938/1.0254mm; increasing the introduced compliance by25% gives1.0485/1.0862mm. Exceeding a conservative bound is not a measured failure.

An alternative physical operation is to compare the actual opposing pad lands locally while the original joint still retains the workpiece. A calibrated removable gauge can establish separation; shoes are positively locked and every gauge is withdrawn before the boundary may be treated as isolated. Simultaneous opposed low-force probing can reduce the workpiece movement caused by establishing that datum. This does not construct the guide, gauge insertion/withdrawal, positive lock or observations. A point or three-point plane does not bound unknown roughness between points. Whole-land figure, tilt, wear and contamination remain indispensable. A gauge is itself a temporary connecting path until retrieved.

For the six declared positions/directions below, let J map rigid workpiece pose q=(translation,rotation) to scalar line motion, and W=transpose(J) map signed line forces to wrench. Set u=(translation,L*rotation),L=.3m, and Jn=[n,(r cross n)/L]. Introduce, rather than infer from any producer artifact, retained-old-joint stiffness Kold=1MN/m times the identity in these normalized coordinates. Two opposed1N probes at each line, each with at most.1N force error, leave signed residual at most.2N per line. Enumerating all64 sign corners of q=Kold^-1*transpose(Jn)*p bounds datum relaxation at the six lands by2.23778,2.23778,1.04667,.63333,1.25556,.468um. If every datum is established under the same bounded simultaneous probing state, these are conditional relaxation terms after removing the probes. Arbitrary sequential probing with changing constraints is not covered.
